query: Does a market maker sell (buy) at a bid or ask price?

Rather, the investors set the price every time it trades. There's no ""official"" price -- just the last trade. "This is a misconception. One of the explanations is that if you buy at the ask price and want   to sell it right away, you can only sell at the bid price. This is incorrect. There are no two separate bid and ask prices. The price you buy (your ""bid"") is the same price someone else sells (their ""sell"").
